as_told.title: Sheehan defends Mack before the Harvard faculty committee

plain: Harvard is said to have tried to push out John Mack, a Harvard psychiatry professor who took the subject of alien encounters seriously, and Mack fought back. Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon intelligence official, tells Michels that Harvard tried to get rid of "that poor Harvard Professor" and that Mack "won a law case" after he "had to go to court." The author Whitley Strieber, who has written of his own encounters, repeats what Mack told him: he was invited to a meeting that was "actually an ambush," where they meant to "take away my license to practice psychiatry." Danny Sheehan, a lawyer, says he was part of it himself: when Mack "got confronted by this faculty committee" he called Sheehan and asked him to represent him. If true, it would show a top university punishing a scholar for studying the subject. The three agree that Harvard moved against Mack, but differ on the form it took: a court case, an ambush meeting over his licence, or a faculty committee.
